# Tool Landscape and Taxonomy

## Static Call Graph Tools

| Tool | Stars | Last Release | Python Support | Status | Approach |
|------|-------|-------------|----------------|--------|----------|
| PyCG [14] | 365 | Nov 2023 (archived) | 3.4+ | Archived | Inter-procedural fixpoint iteration |
| pyan3 [15] | 418 | v2.5.0, Apr 2026 | 3.10-3.14 | Active | AST + symtable |
| JARVIS [17] | N/A | Research artifact | N/A | Research | Flow-sensitive type graphs |
| code2flow [37] | N/A | N/A | Multi-language | Active | AST to flowchart |
| Decoder [36] | N/A | 2025 | N/A | New | AST → SQLite |
| InferCG [4] | N/A | 2025 | N/A | Research | Static + LLM hybrid |

### PyCG

Generates call graphs via inter-procedural analysis computing all assignment
relations between program identifiers [1]. Handles higher-order functions,
complex inheritance, nested definitions, and automatic module discovery [14].
Outputs JSON adjacency lists and FASTEN format [14]. Zero pip dependencies [14].

Archived November 2023 with the statement: "Due to limited availability, no
further development improvements are planned" [14]. Despite being archived,
remains the most-cited baseline in academic literature [2][3][9].

### pyan3

Performs "rather superficial" static analysis using AST and symtable to construct
a directed graph of objects and their define/use relationships [15]. Supports
modern Python syntax including walrus operator, match statements, async with,
and type aliases [15]. Outputs DOT, SVG, HTML, TGF, yEd XML, and plain text
[15]. `--module-level` flag switches to import dependency analysis [15].

### JARVIS

Constructs call graphs "on-the-fly" using function-scoped type graphs with
flow-sensitive intra-procedural analysis [2]. Eliminates the costly global
fixed-point iterations that cause PyCG to fail at scale [2]. Handles context
managers, built-in types, and control flow constructs that PyCG does not [2][17].

### Decoder

Parses Python AST and stores the call graph in a local SQLite file, enabling
querying of full call chains with execution context (conditionals, loops,
try/except) [36]. Announced on Hacker News in 2025 [36].

### InferCG

Hybrid framework combining coarse-grained static analysis with LLM-based
semantic reasoning [4]. Addresses limitations in Python static analysis where
traditional methods fail on dynamic features [4]. Published in ACM TOSEM [4].

## Dynamic Call Graph Tools

| Tool | Stars | Last Release | Python Support | Status | Approach |
|------|-------|-------------|----------------|--------|----------|
| pycallgraph [18] | N/A | Abandoned | 2.7+, 3.3+ | Abandoned | sys.settrace |
| python-call-graph [20] | N/A | Active fork | 3.8-3.13 | Active | sys.settrace |
| VizTracer [31] | N/A | Active | 3.x | Active | sys.settrace + Chrome trace |
| py-spy [21] | N/A | Active | Any | Active | Sampling (Rust) |
| Hunter [22] | N/A | Active | 3.x | Active | sys.settrace + Cython |

### pycallgraph / python-call-graph

Original pycallgraph uses sys.settrace() to generate runtime call graphs [18].
Output formats: Graphviz, Gephi (GDF), JSON [19]. Customizable colors based on
call count, time, or memory usage [18]. Module grouping support [18].

The original is abandoned with multiple forks [18]. The `python-call-graph`
fork supports Python 3.8-3.13 [20].

### VizTracer

Low-overhead tracing and visualization tool that displays every function with
entry/exit timestamps [31][32]. Generates Chrome trace format for browser-based
interactive visualization [64]. Supports multi-thread and multi-process tracing
on a single timeline [31].

### py-spy

Sampling profiler written in Rust [21]. Default 100 Hz sampling rate [21].
Generates interactive SVG flamegraphs with search, zoom, and hover [21]. Does
not run in the same process as the profiled program — attaches externally [21].
Approximately 1% overhead [21].

## Dead Code Detection Tools

| Tool | Approach | Key Feature |
|------|----------|-------------|
| Vulture [30] | AST analysis | 60-100% confidence scores |
| deadcode | AST + call graph | Scope/namespace tracking |

Vulture assigns confidence values to dead code findings but generates high
false positive rates on dynamic code — 59 false positives on a codebase with
zero real issues [66]. Whitelist files are the recommended mitigation [30].

## Gaps and Limitations

- PyCG's archival leaves no actively maintained, academically rigorous static
  call graph tool [14]. JARVIS exists only as a research artifact [17].
- Pyan3 self-describes its analysis as "rather superficial" [15].
- Static tools outperform LLMs significantly for call graph generation [3],
  but the static tool ecosystem is fragmented.
- The distinction between call graph tools (function-level) and dependency
  graph tools (module-level) is important: they serve different analysis needs
  despite superficial similarity.
